questions.question: Samreen and Garima completed a piece of work together in 8 days. If Samreen can complete the same work in 10 days working independently, in how many days will Garima complete the same work alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Samreen + Garima = 8 days,

Samreen alone = 10 days

**Concept:**

1/(Garima's time) = 1/(Samreen + Garima's time) - 1/(Samreen's time)

**Solution:**

⇒ 1/(Garima's time) = 1/8 - 1/10

⇒ (5 - 4)/40 = 1/40

⇒ Garima's time = 40 days

**Hence, Garima can complete the same work alone in 40 days.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 18 days and 36 days respectively. They work together for 8 days and then A leaves. How many days will B take to complete the rest of the work?
questions.solution:
**Given data:

A can complete work in 18 days.

B can complete work in 36 days.

They work together for 8 days.

Concept Used:**

The speed of work is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work.

If A and B work together for a while and then only B continues,

we can subtract the work done by both to find out the remaining work for B.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A in a day = 1/18

⇒ Work done by B in a day = 1/36

⇒ Work done by A and B in a day = 1/18 + 1/36 = 1/12

⇒ Work done by A and B in 8 days = 8/12 = 2/3

⇒ Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3

⇒ Time taken by B to complete the remaining work = (1/3) / (1/36) = 12 days

**Hence, B will take 12 days to complete the rest of the work.**

questions.question: Kuldeep is twice as efficient as Manish to do a work. Working together they can finish a piece of work in 36 days. Kuldeep alone can finish the work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Kuldeep is twice as efficient as Manish.

Working together they can finish a piece of work in 36 days.

**Concept used: **

Work = Efficiency x Time.

**Solution:**

If Manish's efficiency is 1 unit per day, Kuldeep's efficiency is 2 units per day.

Total work = (1 unit/day + 2 units/day) x 36 days = 108 units.

Time taken by Kuldeep alone to finish the work = total work / Kuldeep's efficiency = 108 units / 2 units/day = 54 days.

**Therefore, Kuldeep alone can finish the work in 54 days.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 40 days and B can do the same work in 80 days. They work together for 20 days, how much of the work is left to complete?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Work rate of A (Ra) = 1/40 work/day Work rate of B (Rb) = 1/80 work/day

Together, their combined work rate (Rc) is:

Rc = Ra + Rb = 1/40 + 1/80 = 1/40 + 2/80 = 3/80 work/day

If they work together for 20 days, the fraction of the work they complete (Wc) is:

Wc = Rc * t = 3/80 * 20 = 3/4 of the work

So if 3/4 of the work is complete, the fraction of the work left (Wl) is:

**Wl = 1 - Wc = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4 of the work is left to complete.**

questions.question: Raj is 20 percent less efficient than Rahul. If Rahul can make a computer in 20 days, then Raj can make the same computer in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Efficiency of Raj = 80% of Rahul's efficiency

Rahul can make a computer in 20 days

**Formula Used:**

If efficiency decreases by x%, then time increases by (100)/(100-x) %

**Calculation:**

Efficiency of Raj = 100% - 20% = 80%

Time taken by Rahul = 20 days

Time taken by Raj = (100)/(80) × Time taken by Rahul

Time taken by Raj = (100)/(80) × 20

Time taken by Raj = (100times 20)/(80)

Time taken by Raj = (2000)/(80)

Time taken by Raj = 25 days

Raj can make the same computer in 25 days.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a work in 10 days, B and C together can finish the same work in 15 days, and A and C together can finish the same work in 20 days. In how many days can c alone finish the same work?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

If a person can do a task in x days then in 1 day work will be completed 1/x part

**Calculation:**

1/A + 1/B = 1/10

1/B + 1/C = 1/15

1/A + 1/C = 1/20

Then,

⇒ 1/A - 1/C = 1/30

Solving,

⇒ 1/C = 1/120

**∴ In 120 days, C alone can finish the work.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Calculation:

The combined efficiency of A & B = 60/10 = 6 units

The combined efficiency of B & C = 60/15 = 4 units

The combined efficiency of A & C = 60/ 20 = 3 units

Total efficiency = 2(A + B +C) = 13 (6 + 4 + 3)

⇒ Total efficiency (A + B + C) = 13/2 = 6.5 units

Each efficiency of A = (6.5 - 4) = 2.5 units

Efficiency of B = (6.5 - 3) = 3.5 units.

Efficiency of C = (6.5 - 6) = 0.5 units.

Time taken by C alone to complete the task = 60/(0.5) = 120 days.

**∴ C alone finish the same work in 120 days.**

questions.question: Two persons P and Q working together can do a piece of work in 36 days. Q alone can do it in 45 days. Q alone start the work and left the work after 5 days. How many days will P take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Given:

P + Q's time = 36 days

Q's time = 45 days

Q worked alone for 5 days

**Concept:**

Work done is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work.

**Solution:**

P's time = (P + Q's time) × (Q's time)/(Q's time - P + Q's time) ⇒ 36 × 45/(45 - 36) = 180 days

Work done by Q in 5 days = 5/Q's time ⇒ 5/45 of the total work

Remaining work = 1 - 5/45 = 40/45 of the total work

Time for P to complete the remaining work = Remaining work × P's time ⇒ (40/45) × 180 = 160 days

**Therefore, P will take 160 days to complete the remaining work.**

questions.solution:

Atul's time to complete the work = 114 days

Required time to complete the work = 19 days

questions.question: R and S can complete a work in 15 days and 60 days respectively. They work on alternate days one at a time and R works on the first day. In how many days the whole work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R can complete the work in 15 days.

S can complete the work in 60 days.

They work on alternate days, and R works on the first day.

**Formula Used:**

Work done per day by R = 1/15

Work done per day by S = 1/60

Total work = 1

**Calculation:**

Work done in 2 days = (Work done by R in 1 day) + (Work done by S in 1 day)

Work done in 2 days = 1/15 + 1/60

⇒ Work done in 2 days = (4 + 1)/60

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 5/60

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 1/12

Let the total number of days be 2n (since they work on alternate days).

In 2n days, work done = n × (1/12)

Since the entire work is to be completed, we set the work done to 1.

⇒ n × (1/12) = 1

⇒ n = 12

Total number of days = 2n = 24 days

**The whole work will be completed in 24 days.**

Efficiency Ratio = Work done by Sharman / Work done by Vivek

Time = Work / Efficiency

Efficiency of Sharman = 0.8 unit/day (20% less than Vivek)

Time taken by Vivek to make 1 helmet = 20 days

Work done by Vivek in making 1 helmet = 20 days × 1 unit/day = 20 units

Time taken by Sharman to make the same helmet:

⇒ Time = 20 units / 0.8 units/day

⇒ Time = 25 days

**Sharman can make the same helmet in 25 days.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 72 days and B in 90 days. They worked together for 30 days and then B left. Find the days taken by A to finish the remaining work.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete work in 72 days

B can complete work in 90 days

They work together for 30 days

**Concept/Formula Used:**

Work done = Rate * Time,

where rate is the amount of work one can do in one day.

**Calculation:**

Let's define the rates of A and B (i.e., the fraction of the work they complete in one day):

⇒ A's rate = 1/72 (work/day)

⇒ B's rate = 1/90 (work/day)

Combined, they can do (1/72 + 1/90) of the work in a day:

⇒ Combined rate = 1/72 + 1/90 = (90 + 72) / (72 × 90) = 162/6480 = 1/40 (work/day)

In 30 days, they will complete 30 × (1/40) of the work:

⇒ Work completed together = 30 × (1/40) = 30/40 = 3/4 of the work

This leaves (1 - 3/4) = 1/4 of the work to be done by A alone.

To find out how many days A will take to finish the remaining work, we divide the remaining work by A's rate:

⇒ Remaining days = remaining work / A's rate = (1/4) / (1/72) = 18 days

**Therefore, A will take 18 more days to finish the remaining work.**

questions.question: Preeti alone can complete a work in 30 days and Payal alone can complete the same work in 90 days. Payal alone worked for first 18 days and then left the work. In how many days will Preeti alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Preeti alone can complete the work in 30 days.

Payal alone can complete the same work in 90 days.

Payal worked for the first 18 days and then left.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by a person in one day = 1 / Number of days to complete the work

Total work done = Work done per day × Number of days worked

**Calculation:**

Work done by Payal in one day = 1 / 90

Work done by Payal in 18 days = 18 × (1 / 90)

Work done by Payal in 18 days = 18 / 90

Work done by Payal in 18 days = 1 / 5

Remaining work = 1 - (1 / 5)

Remaining work = 4 / 5

Work done by Preeti in one day = 1 / 30

Let the number of days Preeti needs to complete the remaining work be x.

Work done by Preeti in x days = x × (1 / 30)

Since Preeti completes the remaining work:

⇒ x × (1 / 30) = 4 / 5

⇒ x = (4 / 5) × 30

⇒ x = 24

**Preeti will complete the remaining work in 24 days.**

Work = Men × Time

Work done by 12 men in t hours:

questions.question: Amar is 10 percent more efficient than Sachin. If Sachin alone can finish a work in 44 days, then in how many days can Amar finish the same work
questions.solution:

**Concept:**

Efficiency and Work Relationship: If one person is more efficient than another by a certain percentage, it means they can complete the same amount of work in less time.

**Formula Used:**

If person A is x% more efficient than person B, then the time taken by A to complete the work is:

⇒ Time taken by A = Time taken by B / (1 + x/100)

**Calculation:**

Let the time taken by Amar to complete the work be T days.

Given Sachin takes 44 days and Amar is 10% more efficient:

⇒ T = 44 / (1 + 10/100)

⇒ T = 44 / 1.1

⇒ T = 40 days

questions.question: L alone can complete a work in 200 hours. M alone can complete the same work in 150 hours. L, M and N together can complete the same work in 60 hours. In how many hours can N alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiencies of L, M and N be l, m and n respectively.

One-day efficiency of L : l = 1/200

One-day efficiency of M : m = 1/150

Combined one-day efficiency : l + m + n = 1/60

Substituting values of l and m, we get

1/200 + 1/150 + 1/n = 1/60

1/n = 1/60 - 1/150 - 1/200 = (10 - 4 - 3)/600 = 3/600 = 1/200

∴ N can do the work in 200 hours.

questions.question: F and M together can do a piece of work in 8 days. F alone can do the same work in 12 days. In how many days can M alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Days for M alone = (Product of days) ÷ (Difference of days)

Required time = (12 × 8) ÷ (12 − 8)

Required time = 96 ÷ 4 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by F and M = 8 days; Time taken by F = 12 days.

Combined Work Formula

If A can complete work in x days and B in y days, then together they finish in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work-Efficiency Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. For constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

Alternate Day Work

For work done on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and divide total work by cycle efficiency.</p
